workflow.title: Clean Doctor on Mac: decide between junk files and photo-library cleanup
workflow.primaryIntent: A Mac owner who remembers Clean Doctor needs to identify AI Cleaner Max and distinguish expendable cache investigation from original photo/video/contact cleanup.
workflow.conclusion: Start with the data and device, not the one-click label. The current Mac listing covers both junk and personal-data tools; Breathing Room is a different investigation/review workflow, not a verified duplicate-media replacement.
outline: Identify the same Apple app ID and select the Mac store view, not the phone description.
Separate system/cache candidates, unwanted apps, original media and contacts into different decisions.
Before changing anything, identify backup/sync consequences and the proposed action's recovery path; competitor deletion semantics remain unverified.
Choose photo/contact tools for that documented job; choose storage-by-project/app and activity investigation when that is the actual Mac problem, with the disclosed Breathing Room preview caveats.
Record free space separately from candidate sizes and Trash movements; no measured savings or speed claims.
workflow.visualPlacement: Required competitor Mac UI immediately after lead once cleared and inspected; Breathing Room Space example-data preview beside the storage-investigation branch.
workflow.interactionPass: A non-destructive decision aid: device = Mac/iPhone; target = originals/contacts or rebuildable cache/app data; known recovery path = yes/unknown. Unknown routes to stop and review, not deletion. No filesystem access or unsupported product feature assertions.
workflow.boundary: Provisional intent, not researched keyword demand or a runnable tutorial. Verify any Apple Photos/sync instructions against official Apple documentation before including procedural steps. No obligatory code demo.
